Main.sentence: South Shore is one of 77 defined ___E:community areas of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago)___ , ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ , United States.

Located on the city's ___E:South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side,_Chicago)___ , the area is named for its location along the city's southern ___E:lakefront U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ .

Although South Shore has seen a greater than 40% decrease in residents since Chicago's population peaked in the 1950s, the area remains one of the most densely populated neighborhoods on the South Side.  The community benefits from its location along the waterfront, its accessibility to ___E:Lake Shore Drive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Shore_Drive)___ , and its proximity to major institutions and attractions such as the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ , the ___E:Museum of Science and Industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago))___ , and ___E:Jackson Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Park_(Chicago))___ .

Like all of the City of Chicago, the South Shore community area was originally inhabited by a number of ___E:Algonquian peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_peoples)___ , including the ___E:Mascouten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascouten)___ and ___E:Miami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_(tribe))___ .

After the expulsion of ___E:Native Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States)___ by white settlers in the nineteenth century, it became characterized by small settlements including Essex, Bryn Mawr, Parkside, Cheltenham Beach, and Windsor Park.  The area is bounded by 67th and 79th streets to the north and south and by ___E:Stony Island Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stony_Island_Avenue)___ and ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ to the west and east. In 1861, the ___E:Illinois General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_General_Assembly)___ incorporated ___E:Hyde Park Township U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park_Township,_Cook_County,_Illinois)___ , which included South Shore.

The area's population grew as workers in the nearby ___E:steel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel)___ industry settled in the area.  Following the June 29, 1889 elections, the South Shore community area was annexed into the City of Chicago with the entirety of Hyde Park Township.

The location of the ___E:World's Columbian Exposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World%27s_Columbian_Exposition)___ in nearby Jackson Park prompted the sale of land and building lots. As in other parts of Chicago, the desire for ___E:affordable housing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_housing)___ at the start of the twentieth century led to the large scale construction of ___E:bungalows U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungalows)___ .
Unlike other areas in which bungalows were built en masse, South Shore's bungalow residents were largely ___E:affluent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_upper_class)___ .

Additionally, South Shore was the destination for ___E:white flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_flight)___ from ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(community_area),_Chicago)___ as immigrants and African Americans moved there.
After racially restrictive covenants were declared unconstitutional by Shelley v. Kraemer , African American families began to move into historically white neighborhoods such as South Shore.
The South Shore Commission initiated a program they called "managed integration", designed to check the physical decline of the community and to achieve racial balance.
The initiative was largely unsuccessful on both counts.
Per the 1950 census, South Shore had 79,000 residents and was 96% white.
A 1951 ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ study estimated that over 20% of the neighborhood's residents were Jewish.
In 1960, the population had dropped to 73,000 residents and was 90% white and 10% black.
Like many other urban neighborhoods across the United States undergoing racial change and tensions, many of the white residents began to choose to move to new locations.
By 1970, the population had risen to 81,000 and was 69% black and 28% white as South Shore itself became a victim of ___E:white flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_flight)___ .
By 1980, the population had fallen slightly to 78,000, but was 94% black.
By the late 1990s South Shore had developed into a ___E:middle-class U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_middle_class)___ African American community.
The ___E:Chicago Park District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Park_District)___ purchased the waning South Shore Country Club in 1972, converting it into a cultural center.
The Jackson Park Highlands District is a sixteen block area bounded by East 67th Street on the north.
East 71st Street on the south, South Cregier Avenue on the west, and South Jeffrey Boulevard on the east.
The Jackson Park Highlands District is a historic district in the South Shore community area of Chicago.
The district was built in 1905 by various architects.
It was designated a Chicago Landmark on October 25, 1989.
The Jeffery–Cyril Historic District is a national historic district in the South Shore neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois.
The district comprises a cluster of six apartment buildings on Jeffery Boulevard, 71st Place, and Cyril Avenue.

All six buildings were built between 1927 and 1929.  The district was added to the ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ on May 5, 1986.
The South Shore Bungalow Historic District is a residential historic district in the South Shore neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois.

The district contains 229 Chicago bungalows and twenty other residential buildings built between 1911 and 1930. The district was added to the ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ on December 10, 2008.

The ___E:South Shore Cultural Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore_Cultural_Center)___ , previously the South Shore Country Club, began as a lakefront retreat for the wealthiest of Chicago's movers and shakers.

The firm of ___E:Marshall and Fox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_and_Fox)___ , architects of the Drake, Blackstone, and Edgewater Beach hotels, were hired to design an opulent, Mediterranean-style clubhouse for a membership that included some of Chicago's most prominent families.
The grounds provided private stables and members-only beach, and golf course.

Tennis, horseback riding, and ___E:skeet shooting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeet_shooting)___ were enjoyed by guests the likes of ___E:Jean Harlow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Harlow)___ , ___E:Will Rogers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Rogers)___ , and ___E:Amelia Earhart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Earhart)___ .

Between the first and second World Wars, a housing boom brought a development of luxury cooperative apartments and mansions to the neighborhood surrounding the club. In 1974 the club held its last members-only event.
The Chicago Park District owns the property.
It has been restored to its original design and is open to the public.

A major drawback [according to whom?] to the South Shore and surrounding ___E:South Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Chicago)___ neighborhoods is that they are one of the few remaining Chicago lakefront neighborhoods that lack a fully publicly ___E:accessible neighborhood shoreline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_beaches#South_Shore_Beaches)___ .
There are lakefront gaps between the existing South Shore Cultural Center and Rainbow Beach to its south.

Even larger masses of lakefront land along the South Chicago neighborhood (at the abandoned USX steel mill), which overlook the city's lakefront and Chicago skyline, are [when?] undergoing development as parks and not completely available for recreational use by the adjacent neighborhood residents. [citation needed] Presently, [when?] ___E:Chicago Lakeside Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Lakeside_Development)___ has proposed plans that call for the completion of this southern portion of lakefront with the development of new parklands, beaches, and a continuous waterfront bicycle and jogging path that will link ___E:Calumet Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_Park)___ and Beach in the ___E:East Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Side,_Chicago)___ neighborhood to the South Shore Cultural Center in South Shore. [needs update] Completion of such a project would [citation needed] result in improved access to Chicago's southern lakefront and connect it to neighborhoods such as ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ and ___E:Bronzeville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas,_Chicago#Bronzeville)___ to the north. [citation needed]

At the northern end of South Shore is the historic district Jackson Park Highlands, one of Chicago's greatest [according to whom?] examples of structural history and 19th-century architecture, with a number of homes in the style of ___E:American Foursquare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Foursquare)___ , ___E:Colonial Revival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Revival_architecture)___ , and ___E:Renaissance Revival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Revival_architecture)___ on suburban-sized lots. [citation needed]
Located in the Bryn Mawr section of South Shore is the ___E:Allan Miller House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Miller_House)___ at 7121 South Paxton Avenue.

Commissioned by advertising executive Allan Miller, this home is an example of ___E:Prairie-style architecture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie_School)___ in the area. Built in 1915, it is Chicago's only surviving building designed by John Van Bergen, a former member of ___E:Frank Lloyd Wright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lloyd_Wright)___ 's architecture firm. [citation needed]

The South Shore community area has supported the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ in the past two presidential elections by overwhelming margins.

In the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2016)___ , the South Shore cast 18,130 votes for ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ and cast 373 votes for ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ (96.07% to 1.98%).

In the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2012)___ , South Shore cast 22,515 votes for ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and cast 222 votes for ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ (98.77% to 0.97%).

On July 14, 2018, the community clashed with the ___E:Chicago Police Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Police_Department)___ after a local barber, Harith Augustus, was shot multiple times by a police officer at 71st Street and Chappel Avenue. ___E:Body camera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_camera)___ footage without audio was released immediately contrary to past practices of months-long waits for video in other police shootings.
Footage taken by body cameras of other officers has not been released.

The ___E:Nation of Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Islam)___ National Center and ___E:Mosque Maryam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosque_Maryam)___ are at 7351 South Stony Island Avenue.
The ___E:National Black United Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Black_United_Front)___ has its headquarters in the community.
The ___E:Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Chicago)___ operates Catholic churches.

On July 1, 2020, Our Lady of Peace, St. Bride, and St. Philip Neri in South Shore and Our Lady Gate of Heaven Church in ___E:Jeffery Manor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffery_Manor,_Chicago)___ will merge.
The South Shore community area has five stations along the South Chicago Branch of the ___E:Metra Electric District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ .

In South Shore, the South Chicago Branch runs the median of along East 71st Street, making stops at ___E:Stony Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stony_Island_station)___ , ___E:Bryn Mawr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryn_Mawr_station_(Metra))___ , and ___E:South Shore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore_station)___ stations before turning southeast along South Exchange Avenue to make stops at ___E:Windsor Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Park_station)___ and ___E:Cheltenham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham_station_(Metra))___ stations.

In addition, the ___E:75th Street station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/75th_Street_(Grand_Crossing)_station)___ is on the ___E:Greater Grand Crossing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Grand_Crossing,_Chicago)___ side of the border between that area and South Shore.
___E:Chicago Public Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Public_Schools)___ operates district public schools.
___E:Urban Prep Academies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Prep_Academies)___ has a South Shore Campus.

___E:Muhammad University of Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_University_of_Islam)___ , a ___E:Nation of Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Islam)___ -affiliated primary and secondary school, is adjacent to the Mosque Maryam.
